nodes.statement: The test fills the bounded local allocator before requesting another layer group.
The bounded flow uses a complete two-layer group, fixed capacity, and busy_loop disabled.
The flow enters batched_allocate for the initial layer group.
The local CPU backend delegates batched allocation to its mixed-memory allocator.
The initial allocation returns MemoryObj resources for every layer in the group.
submit_put_task increments each MemoryObj reference and stores it in hot_cache under its key.
Pinning one object makes its complete layer group ineligible for eviction.
Under pressure, candidate validation finds no complete evictable group while the group is pinned.
With busy_loop disabled and no complete candidate, batched_allocate returns None.
The caller releases the pin before retrying allocation.
The retry evicts the complete old group, removes its keys, and batched-frees its MemoryObj resources.
Freed capacity lets the retry allocate replacement MemoryObj resources for the layer group.
After recovery, old keys are absent and allocator memcheck succeeds.
The pinned-failure and unpin-retry test observes both the initial None result and successful recovery.

edges.statement: Filling the fixed-capacity allocator establishes the pressure precondition for the nonbusy two-layer request.
The bounded two-layer request is passed to batched_allocate.
The backend allocation entry delegates to the mixed-memory allocator.
The delegated initial allocation acquires one MemoryObj per requested layer.
Putting each allocated object increments its reference and transfers a retained reference into hot_cache.
A retained hot-cache object is pinned, making its group non-evictable.
The pinned member prevents selection of the complete layer group under allocation pressure.
With no complete eviction candidate and nonbusy mode, allocation returns None.
The failed allocation preserves the group so the caller can unpin it before retrying.
Unpinning makes the old complete group eligible for eviction and batched free on retry.
Freeing the old group restores enough capacity for replacement allocation.
Successful replacement allocation follows removal of old keys and leaves allocator accounting consistent.
The recovery test asserts old-key absence and allocator memcheck after retry.

disconfirming_checks.statement: A failed nonbusy allocation must not remove keys from the pinned group.
When another complete group is evictable, the allocator evicts that safe group rather than the pinned group.
